definition: The task of producing a shorter version of a text that captures its most important information.
details: Summarization approaches include extractive methods (selecting existing sentences from the source) and abstractive methods (generating new sentences that paraphrase and condense the source), with modern LLMs primarily excelling at the latter.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is Text Summarization.
